title: 49ers, Kyle Shanahan agreed to contract extension in offseason: Source
content:
The San Francisco 49ers signed head coach Kyle Shanahan to a contract extension earlier this past offseason, a team source said on condition of anonymity because the transaction has not been announced publicly. Details about the contract were not disclosed.

Shanahan, 46, is in his 10th season coaching the 49ers. San Francisco’s 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, in the season opener was his 150th regular-season game with the team, two shy of Bill Walsh for the most in franchise history. The 49ers are 83-67 in those games.

He has also appeared in 14 playoff games, matching Walsh’s total, going 9-5 with two Super Bowl appearances (both losses to the Kansas City Chiefs) and two other trips to the NFC Championship Game.

Shanahan was limited during training camp this summer after suffering a concussion and other injuries in a July car wreck. He steadily resumed his typical duties during the preseason.

The timing of the contract news is such that it seems like a reward for the thorough win over the Rams, and the 49ers were clearly the better-coached and more prepared team in that game. But the team’s ownership, front office and players have long regarded Shanahan as not only one of the very best offensive play callers in the league, but also a coach who handles players well and gets the most out of them.

Shanahan has also worked well with general manager John Lynch, who seemingly has an open-ended deal with owner Jed York to do this as long as he wants. Shanahan and Lynch often talk about their abilities to bounce ideas off each other and be critical when necessary.

No story about a Shanahan extension would be complete without mention of quarterback Brock Purdy. The development of the last player taken in the 2022 draft is a huge reason the 49ers are winning games, and that both Shanahan and Lynch are not regularly ridiculed for trading three first-round draft picks in 2021 to take Trey Lance.
